target_customer: Spreadsheet users and small businesses/developers using API data for reports, recruiting and sales lists (pricing from $29/month by 2019)
problem: Getting API and web data into Excel and Google Sheets required coding; Blockspring exposed functions as spreadsheet formulas.
business_model: Freemium subscription (from $29/month) plus enterprise private functions

founders.name: Paul Katsen
founders.background_notes: Named CEO in a16z and TechCrunch; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Spreadsheet add-ins and an API function marketplace; modest engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A library of public functions was easy to replicate; no data or network lock-in sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not sourced; no incumbent copy or purchase found. Coinbase acqui-hired the team in 2019.

market_need_then: a16z (2015-07) cites plugins for Excel and Google Sheets and public functions; no usage numbers published.

branding.brand_signature: Spreadsheet formula '=BLOCKSPRING' as the way users call the product (a16z)

brand_strength.rationale: Product name doubled as a spreadsheet function but no sources show brand-driven growth.

pivots.to: API data for lead, recruiting and reporting lists
pivots.why: TechCrunch (2019) says it began as a serverless data business and pivoted; timing and reasons not stated

outcome_analysis: Blockspring raised $3.4M from a16z and SV Angel in 2015 and was acquired by Coinbase in January 2019 in an undisclosed deal TechCrunch called an acqui-hire. Both investors also back Coinbase. It sold a niche product to spreadsheet users; no revenue is public, and the outcome reads as a soft landing rather than a breakout.
notes: Crunchbase total (via TechCrunch) is about $3.5M; one aggregator claims a 2017 Coda acquisition, uncorroborated and ignored. YC page lists Pinkus and Tokoph; a16z and TechCrunch name Katsen as CEO. No competitors dated 2014 found in sources. Name origin not found. Directory status Acquired agrees.
